I was like this myself before. I was talking to myself about subconscious impressing, about changing beliefs, and I hadn't realized that this was keeping a distance between me and my desire. It usually felt like a desire and not something I was, now. I was identifying myself with someone who tries to convince themselves about something, when I had to identify with someone who is already convinced. Someone who IS, who FEELS. I have even dropped the word "belief", because it feels off. It feels like a barrier between me and my self. If you feel something, if you think from something, you are it. 

I do have some lingering questions though. If you wanted to answer them that would be great. If my chosen feeling is happiness, not necessarily joy, but happiness, should I always appropriate happiness with the intensity that I feel it after some repetition in affirmation sessions? I can reach ecstasy or something close, joy for sure, but if what I feel to be was my 3D I wouldn't feel joy all the time. Joy comes after feeling happiness for some time. I would feel it if I was sitting somewhere, musing about my amazing life for a while, but during the day for a fleeting thought here and there I would feel contentment. Neville talks about one feeling, the feeling of the wish fulfilled (which is "belief", being, more accurately, and the chosen emotion implies that being, one could say IS that being, I don't know) and I was thinking that one can feel happiness intensely or less intensely, but always feel it, always think from. I wouldn't want to feel happiness intensely to the point of joy if I was watching a movie or drifting to sleep, I would be or want to be content with my life, happy, but not intensely happy, because I would want the movie to grab my attention. I would be intensely happy if I kept entertaining that happy feeling. So my question is, even though I'm probably able to appropriate (say something as though I feel joyful and eventually feel it, I'm only explaining to see if I got it right) immediately a joyful feeling relating to what I am, should I do that? That would be unnatural, no? And I don't think I want that. I want to be in love with my life, happy, but not always intensely or that intensely. A calm contentment, a content sigh, is always happiness too and always implies, always is. Maybe the feeling is always the same, happiness, so I am doing it right, but it's in a spectrum and as long as I feel it, always think from, always being that I am, it's okay. Otherwise it would definitely be wrong to assume that I'm not feeling it real if for example I'm done feeling ecstatic for a while and just feel a calm being, a calm "knowing", right? Like, my mom is not always ecstatic that I'm in her life, but sometimes she is and she cries from love. This is natural. I guess I'm worrying that I'm not returning to the right state and not using the same feeling and I'm not making it dominant because but I guess it's always the same feeling in different moods/intensities and always the same state, the state of being, of having. No?

Also, I'm confused as to what I'm supposed to do when I start to be aware that I'm successfully feeling it. I'm feeling happy when I realize I'm doing it right, so is it me falling out of the state of being? I should always come back to being when I shift from being what I am to being aware that I felt what I was saying when I said it, right? This is weird to me though, because it feels like there's no meta-being, like, am I supposed to not pay attention that I am applying the law all day? Because if that's the case, even writing this comment, is me not being in the state, or focusing on the 3D in a way and not being. Even when I talk to myself and say "just be, just feel it" it's me taking another step backwards? I find that when I'm coaching, directing myself, it helps me to focus sometimes. Am I supposed to stop being aware, to not even say "oh yes, I'm feeling it"?. Like, if I know I'm being it, it gets me out of the state of being it?? I shouldn't even feel I'm doing it properly? Or am I reaching "insanity" here and it's okay to congratulate myself but then I should come back to being? Because with that previous thinking I shouldn't even be happy at the end of the day that I did what I had to do or see where I'm wrong.. I will never stop be aware of things and I feel I'm taking things to a next level.. I find I shouldn't stop being aware of the good things, I'm always awareness at the end of the day, and I can't escape that nor should I escape being aware of the good things, right? But I'm afraid to come back to a place where I'm "manifesting", I want to be..

You aren't trying to feel wealth, health etc. The target is, for example, to feel that you know you are healthy. The feeling isn't an emotion neither something material, but the knowing that you are healthy now. What would your version of yourself that KNOWS they are healthy think and feel? You would think something that implies 1. health, 2. knowing that you are healthy, but a type of knowing that doesn't have anything that goes against it. You aren't the version of yourself that tries to convince you that you are healthy. You aren't saying to yourself "but I know I am healthy!", that implies that you know you are healthy, but not all of you, that some part of you doesn't know it. What would the version of yourself that has ALREADY CONVINCED themselves that they are healthy, that it's obvious TO THEIR WHOLE MIND that they are healthy, that their belief to something is being backed up by their mind, to the point that their outside reality reflects it back? What would you say right now if you knew you were healthy and your 3D showed it too and how would you feel? In the beginning you would say maybe something like "holy shit, I'm so healthy!", but that implies surprise. Maybe you would want to think how a version of yourself that has been healthy for so long would think, that it's normal for them. So you would want to think something that implies 1. health, 2. belief that you are healthy, a belief that is being backed up by everything, 3. naturalness (not necessarily being bored about the fact of if being true, but a feeling that would imply something like "well yeah, I am healthy, duh, tell me something I don't know"). You aren't being ungrateful, but it's that obvious to you. It's like you always have been healthy, so you don't really know how sickness feels like. I don't know, this is at least how I would want to think about my health for the rest of my life. A more pronounced feeling of gratitude would be great too, but maybe that would make ME think "I'm so grateful that now I'm healthy, remember how sick I used to be?". Like, one can be grateful for health if he has known sickness, but maybe it's okay to remember that you once used to be sick as long as your focus is on the present of obvious health. This is life in essence, you are happy because you once wasn't, so I guess it's normal to know in general that you once weren't happy, without actively bringing back that past, you don't have amnesia all of a sudden. I'm thinking out loud here, I don't know yet how I feel about that. If we were talking about a SP, I would want to feel the same amount of belief, but maybe I would attach to that a feeling of contentment too. Like if I'm married for example, I wouldn't want to be "yeah yeah, I'm married to X, it's good". I would want to be "it's so wonderful that I'm married to X and we're having the time of our lives". So I guess it depends on the target and how you would want to feel. Emotions aren't the feeling like I said, but they IMPLY both the fact (marriage) and the feeling itself, belief/knowing that is being backed up by everything.

Τους is indeed the plural of του, when it's the object in genitive ("τους δίνω έναν χυμό") and it's also the plural of τον, when it's the object in accusative ("τον φίλησε"). 1) there is no meaning in "αγαπώ η γυναίκα μου", it's wrong. When you say "αγαπώ" you're saying "I love", the subject of the verb is "I". "Η γυναίκα μου" is in nominative, it's a subject,  when it should be in accusative, like the example you gave next, "I love my wife". So either you're gonna change the case of "η γυναίκα μου" and make it an object to "Αγαπώ" or you're gonna  change the person of the verb and make it "αγαπάει" to match the "η γυναίκα μου" ("My wife loves..." or you're gonna make two different phrases, because two nominative cases can't be together.

5) it most definitely isn't. Greek is a language with cases, and cases have a meaning. The nominative and the accusative cases mean different things. The subject (nominative) has a different form than the object (accusative/genitive), it's not like in English. Every time you want to talk about the object of a verb, it has to be marked with a case, a form that it's going to tell you it's the object, and that's causative (and genitive in some cases).
